content: The diagnosis of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy (DPN) should follow the guidelines established by the American Diabetes Association (ADA). Annual screening for DPN is recommended for individuals with type 1 diabetes who have had the condition for five or more years, as well as for all individuals with type 2 diabetes, regardless of the duration of their disease. The clinical presentation of DPN can vary depending on the specific types of sensory nerve fibers that are affected. Symptoms may include pain, numbness, tingling, or other sensory abnormalities. Electrophysiological testing, such as nerve conduction studies, is not routinely performed but may be necessary in cases where the clinical features are atypical or unclear. In addition to screening for DPN, it is essential to evaluate for other potential non-diabetic causes of neuropathy. These may include vitamin deficiencies (e.g., vitamin B12 deficiency), infections, or other chronic systemic diseases that could contribute to the patient’s symptoms. Identifying and addressing these alternative causes is a critical component of the diagnostic process.
